excerpt: Course Objective: The course is divided into two ongoing paralleled tracks and will run in a Lab format: Track 1, will basically consist of an introduction to an array of databases and electronic resources that will provide the basis for understanding how to access information on-line. Students will get acquainted with various aspects of the Internet, as well as commercial databases and citation databases. Students will also have the opportunity to explore interactive sources of information such as Listservs, Newsgroups, and Blogs. Lastly, students will be exposed to traditional research methods, including the use of microfilm and microfiche. The emphasis of this track of the course is to have students acquire a working knowledge of how to access information on-line and off-line in order to support their reporting and writing skills. Track 2 consists of an introduction to the basics of building and manipulating data sets. The usage and manipulation of spreadsheets will be presented using Microsoft Excel. Manipulation and exploration of relational databases and database management tools will be covered using Microsoft Access. Thus, the dual emphasis of the course is to have students acquire the basic skills and practical knowledge of how to access information in order to support their reporting practices, as well as, a basic understanding of data managers and spreadsheet software and their fundamental relationship to present day journalistic practice. The above stated objectives will be explored and achieved through in-class assignments, exercises, quizzes, etc. Class work will be based on the assigned readings and exercises from the required textbook, online links, and class handouts. In addition, there will be a "partnered" project assigned. Students will be paired off and and assigned a “partnered” project that will culminate in a “news story” based on the exploration and compilation of data based on online research, spreadsheet manipulation using Microsoft Excel, and assimilation of data from various data sets using Microsoft Access. Measurable Outcomes: 1. Proficiency in online and off-line research . 2. Basic understanding and functional knowledge of Microsoft Excel. 3. Basic understanding and functional knowledge of Microsoft Access. 4. A grasp of essential basic math/statistical principles. 5. Fundamentals of "boolean" searching.
